comparator.name: Human Resource Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Appendix I confirms the Dutch full-time Personeelwetenschappen track, with 60 EC in each year. The 30 EC mobility window permits combinations of placement, minor and electives. Coaching and Development is the first of two equal professionalisation choices; the English People Management track has a different curriculum.

components.name: Professional Skills in Human Resource Studies
components.note: GROW mentoring and personal development continue across the programme and carry no credits.

components.name: Academic Writing in Human Resource Studies A
Social Psychology for the Social Sciences
Introduction to Statistics
components.note: The ordinary first-year binding study advice threshold is 42 EC.

components.name: Academic Writing in Human Resource Studies B
Mobility Window: Minor, Placement or Electives
components.note: Choose a combination of placement, minor and/or electives for 30 EC in total, at Tilburg or abroad. The comparison leaves this content open.

components.name: Coaching and Development
components.note: Choose one 6 EC course: Coaching and Development or Managing Teams and Social Capital. This example uses the first-listed choice.

components.name: The Future of Work: Sustainable and Critical Perspectives
Social Philosophy for Human Resource Studies
Bachelor’s Thesis in Human Resource Studies
components.note: Entry to the bachelor thesis requires 120 EC. This pathway earns those credits by the end of year two.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option addresses organisational behaviour, evidence-based decisions and strategic and financial context. The second develops psychological health and development; the third develops institutions and policy affecting organisations and work. These are different curricular priorities, with each pair exceeding the four-course floor. No fourth option is considered.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both address survey design, psychological measurement and analysis; UCR uses leadership and social-experience applications.
Both examine motivation, teams, leadership and organisational culture.
Both introduce sociological theories and apply them to social life.
Both develop qualitative design, data collection and interpretation.
Both examine social influence, group behaviour and social psychological research.
Both develop statistical analysis for social and behavioural data.
Both study stress, health behaviour and well-being; UCR focuses on health and illness more broadly than the workplace.
Both address financial and management-accounting decisions; UCR does not specialise in personnel costs.
Both teach empirical design, operationalisation, measurement and introductory analysis.
Both introduce economic reasoning about markets and economic decisions.
Both address organisational strategy; UCR emphasises digital transformation.

notes.text: Tilburg offers a dedicated sequence in HR strategy, labour law, work and health, personnel assessment, consulting and HR analytics, followed by a required thesis. UCR combines related courses in organisations, psychological health and research, or institutions and policy. Its options do not reproduce the full specialist HRM sequence.
The Tilburg track teaches primarily in Dutch, with some courses in English. UCR teaches in English.

audience.programmeDescription: Human Resource Studies at Tilburg University examines people, work and organisations. It connects personnel policy and organisational performance with employee well-being, drawing on psychology, sociology, management, economics and law.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers related study through organisations and strategy, psychological health and development, or institutions and policy. Tilburg provides more specialised sequences in HRM, labour law, personnel assessment and people analytics, alongside a required thesis.
